feed.title: OBRAVEN Insights
feed.subtitle: Wind measurement, energy yield, and review – from OBRAVEN Limited

entry.title: Cleaning iced met mast data: the decisions that change the energy yield
entry.summary: Icing turns met mast cleaning into a judgement call. Most of those calls barely touch the energy yield; a few change it, and you can test which.

entry.title: Faster tools expand the search space
entry.summary: Running more layouts, turbines, and constraint cases has got much easier. Knowing what the spread across them means has not.

entry.title: Same 95% availability. Very different years.
entry.summary: A single long-term availability assumption is usually right for the energy estimate. In a year-by-year financial model, the timing can matter.

entry.title: The handover should preserve more than the final number
entry.summary: Model files show what was run. They do not always show why. Reproducible analysis is a commercial asset when a project is sold, financed, or reviewed.

entry.title: The finance-stage EYA may be iteration 50
entry.summary: Most wind projects go through dozens of energy yield iterations before financing. The formal assessment should build on that history.

entry.title: Nearby is not the same as representative
entry.summary: “There is wind data nearby” is a useful start. Whether it represents your turbines and your hub height is a different question.

entry.title: Measurement-efficient, not measurement-free
entry.summary: Model-only bankability in wind is an attractive idea. For lender reliance today, the practical direction is narrower: measured data where it matters.

entry.title: A layout change can save cost and still lose value
entry.summary: Wind project value often sits between disciplines. A turbine move that helps civil design may quietly cost generation.

entry.title: Design the campaign. The kit follows.
entry.summary: A good wind measurement campaign is designed backwards from what the project will need from it. Then the equipment list starts to make sense.
